name: NILM seq2seq: worst-device episode F1 on UK-DALE house_1
objectiveLabel: Target: every device F1 > 0.7 (episode-level, frozen 6 s protocol)

description:
Baseline v1: multi-house pretrained multi-output dilated CNN (house_2+house_5 sources, 80/20 train/val, 40k train + 8k val windows, window 128, stride 32, batch 512, 5 epochs, LR 1e-3, masked MSE + weighted BCE with per-device pos_weight kettle 34.1 / microwave 50.0 / fridge 1.3 / washing_machine 50.0 / dishwasher 1.0).

Eval: house_1 post-split 30d slice, frozen episode protocol (thr half_p50, >=2-sample episodes, tau 12e6 us, dwell_band (1/3, 3.0)).

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 0 / 0.000 / 14.6 / 0.0425
microwave 262 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.3 / 0.0214
fridge 28034 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1166
washing_machine 2966 / 0 / 0.000 / 27.9 / 0.0813
dishwasher 1353 / 0 / 0.000 / 17.0 / 0.0495
pooled F1 0.000; coverage pred=0.000 vs true=0.258.

Diagnosis: training collapsed in epoch 0 - train_mse 2724.57 -> 1.13 flat, val_mse_scaled frozen at 0.05416 across all 5 epochs, BCE noisy (389->110->64->48->85). Model outputs all-zeros (coverage_pred_share=0). Also: RuntimeWarning invalid value in divide at model.py:163 predict overlap-mean (cnt=0 windows -> NaN) - robustness bug to fix.

Next: stabilize training (grad clip, LR 3e-4, more epochs) before i2 calibration fine-tune.
title: EXP-01: multi-house pretrain baseline collapses to zero
summary: All 5 devices n_pred=0; training collapsed in epoch 0 (train_mse 2724.6->1.13, val_mse frozen 0.05416). Baseline min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: i1: multi-house pretraining (house_2+house_5) transfers zero-shot to house_1 eval under the frozen episode protocol.
asi.rollback_reason: n/a - baseline run, kept to anchor the segment.
asi.next_action_hint: Training-stability fix before i2: gradient clipping, LR 3e-4, 15+ epochs; fix NaN divide at model.py:163 (cnt=0 windows). Then calibration fine-tune (K=5 sessions).

description:
i1b training-stability iteration on top of baseline 54cf23b. Changes applied to model.py (exact recipe for re-application):
1. INPUT_SCALE=1000.0: mains watts divided by 1000 both in build_pool training inputs and in predict() input pad (descale unchanged: core*max_w - core is in normalized device units).
2. Power head clamp min=0.0, max=1.5 (target range).
3. Grad clip: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(net.parameters(), 1.0) after backward.
4. LR 1e-3 -> 3e-4, EPOCHS 5 -> 12 (batch 512 unchanged).
5. NaN fix in predict overlap-mean: safe = np.where(cnt>0, acc/np.maximum(cnt,1), 0.0).
6. Added train-end diagnostics print (power head + on-head activity on 2048 val windows).

Result: training no longer collapses. Epoch trace: train_mse 0.13-0.26, bce 9.5->7.95 declining, val_mse_scaled 0.0039-0.0105 (10x below the v1 frozen 0.05416). Diagnostics: power head mean=0.124 max=1.31, on-head mean=0.32 max=1.0.

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / match / P / R / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 30 / 12 / 0.400 / 0.040 / 0.073 / 15.6 / 0.0454
microwave 262 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.4 / 0.0215
fridge 28034 / 2 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1166
washing_machine 2966 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 27.9 / 0.0814
dishwasher 1353 / 1851 / 10 / 0.005 / 0.007 / 0.006 / 27.0 / 0.0788
pooled F1 0.001; coverage pred=0.106 vs true=0.258. mean_mae_w 23.57 (vs 21.36 baseline - slightly worse), worst 40.0 (fridge, unchanged).

Diagnosis: heads are imbalanced across devices - dishwasher hyperactive (1851 preds vs 1353 gt, P=0.005), fridge channel effectively dead (MAE 40.0 = predicting ~0 despite 26% positive rate and pos_weight 1.3). Points to source->target transfer mismatch in per-device output levels, which is exactly what i2 (calibration fine-tune on the K=5 ctx sessions) is designed to fix.

Discarded per loop contract: min_device_f1 0 -> 0 (tie, no primary improvement). The recipe above + this description fully specify re-application.
title: EXP-02: stability fixes revive training, min-device still 0
summary: Input kW scaling + grad clip + LR 3e-4 + 12 epochs: training healthy (val_mse 0.005 vs 0.054 frozen), kettle F1 0.073, dishwasher 0.006; fridge n_pred=2 keeps min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: Stability fixes (input /1000 kW scale, head clamp 1.5, grad clip 1.0, LR 3e-4, 12 epochs, NaN guard) revive training and lift episode F1 off zero for some devices.
asi.rollback_reason: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0; contract keeps only primary improvements. Re-apply recipe from description in the next iteration.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-03 = re-apply the 6 stability changes + i2 calibration fine-tune (K=5 ctx sessions per device) to fix the dead-fridge / hyperactive-dishwasher transfer mismatch. Consider i13 threshold snapping on predict if fine-tune alone is insufficient.

description:
i2 calibration fine-tune on top of re-applied stability recipe (v3 model.py). Stability changes re-applied exactly as documented in run 2 (INPUT_SCALE=1000 input kW scaling in build_pool + predict, head clamp min=0/max=1.5, grad clip 1.0, LR 3e-4, EPOCHS 12, predict NaN guard cnt=0 -> 0).

i2 design: after pretraining, fine-tune the WHOLE net on the K=5 target-house calib sessions per device (25 windows total, each supervising only its own device channel; other channels masked). FT_LR=1e-4, FT_EPOCHS=40, batch 32. Calib data: house_1 PRE-SPLIT (no eval leakage - verified bench.py line 250 pre = load_house(TARGET_HOUSE, None, SPLIT_US)).

Calib window stats: kettle on-frac 0.16, microwave 0.09, fridge 0.76, washing_machine 0.72, dishwasher 0.84 (observed-frac 0.82-0.90).

Fine-tune trace: calib_loss 12.66 -> 1.60 over 40 epochs (memorized the 25 windows). RETENTION DAMAGE: pretrain-val MSE 0.00623 -> 0.07144 (11.5x worse). Calib-fit MSE 0.048.

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / match / P / R / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 303 / 39 / 0.129 / 0.130 / 0.130 / 33.9 / 0.0988
microwave 262 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 7.3 / 0.0214
fridge 28034 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0.000 / 40.0 / 0.1167
washing_machine 2966 / 849 / 128 / 0.151 / 0.043 / 0.067 / 43.3 / 0.1262
dishwasher 1353 / 2011 / 39 / 0.019 / 0.029 / 0.023 / 91.8 / 0.2677
pooled F1 0.011; coverage pred=0.448 vs true=0.258 (over-prediction). mean_mae_w 43.26 (worse than EXP-02 23.57), worst 91.8.

Findings: (1) Target-house adaptation lifts episode F1 for kettle (2x) and washing_machine (new) - the transfer-mismatch hypothesis is directionally right. (2) Weight-space fine-tuning on 25 windows overfits and wrecks overall calibration (MAE doubled, coverage over-predicts 0.448 vs 0.258). (3) Fridge (n_pred=0) and microwave (n_pred=0) stay dead through BOTH stability fixes and fine-tune - not purely a fine-tuning problem.

Discarded: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0. Next hypothesis: keep the stable pretrained net UNTOUCHED (no weight fine-tune) and calibrate the per-device OUTPUT SCALE from the calib sessions (least-squares watts scale on observed calib positions, clamped) - attacks the level mismatch without weight drift; plus diagnostics printing per-device predicted-watts p95 on ON positions vs the frozen threshold to measure how far dead heads are from firing.
title: EXP-03: i2 calib fine-tune helps some devices, overfits
summary: Fine-tune on 25 calib windows: kettle F1 0.073->0.130, wm 0->0.067, but pretrain-val MSE 0.006->0.071 (11x retention damage), MAE 23.6->43.3. Fridge+microwave still 0 -> min_device_f1=0.

asi.hypothesis: i2 weight fine-tune on K=5 calib sessions adapts per-device output levels to the target house and lifts episode F1.
asi.rollback_reason: min_device_f1 tie 0->0 AND fine-tune overfits (retention MSE 11x worse, MAE doubled) - weight-space adaptation on 25 windows is the wrong vehicle; output-space calibration is the fix direction.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-04 = stability recipe (no weight fine-tune) + per-device output-scale calibration from calib (least-squares on observed positions, clamp [0.5, 4.0], applied in predict descale) + diagnostics: per-device pred p95 on ON positions vs frozen threshold. If fridge head has no signal at all, next target the fridge head directly (source-data audit / dedicated head loss).

description:
i9 output-scale calibration on top of the stability recipe (v4 model.py; no weight fine-tune). Stability changes identical to runs 2-3 (documented there). New: per-device least-squares watts scale from calib sessions r_d = sum(p*q)/sum(p*p) on observed positions, clamped [0.5, 4.0], applied in predict descale (core * max_w * r_d); plus calib diagnostics printing per-device predicted-watts p95 on ON positions vs frozen threshold.

NOTE: ft_pretrain_val_mse_pre/post are 0 here = NOT APPLICABLE (v4 dropped the whole-net fine-tune; those metrics belong to the v3 design). washing_machine_f1=0.0 is real (1 predicted episode, 0 matches).

Calib diagnostics (the key evidence):
kettle r=1.08 pred_p95_on=3206W true_p50_on=2331W thr=1173W (ALIVE, over-amplitude)
microwave r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=1588W thr=762W (DEAD)
fridge r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=90W thr=44W (DEAD)
washing_machine r=1.00 pred_p95_on=0W true_p50_on=1778W thr=90W (DEAD)
dishwasher r=1.00 pred_p95_on=2672W true_p50_on=122W thr=60W (ALIVE, fires everywhere)

Result: scales all ~1.0 - multiplicative calibration cannot revive a head that outputs exactly 0W. Per-device table ~= EXP-02: kettle 38 preds F1 0.077, fridge 2, washing_machine 1, microwave 0, dishwasher 1853 F1 0.006. min_device_f1=0, mean_device_f1=0.0167, mean_mae_w=23.60, coverage pred=0.108 vs true=0.258.

Root-cause analysis (from diagnostics + loss structure): (1) The MSE amplitude gradient scales with normalized ON amplitude - fridge ON target is 90/2048=0.044 (negligible gradient) vs kettle 2331/3996=0.58 (strong) -> amplitude-starved heads die. (2) The ON head IS alive (train-end diagnostics: sigmoid mean 0.32 max 1.0) but predict() DISCARDS it (p, _ = net(xb)) - detection is currently expected from the MSE power head alone, which is the wrong vehicle for rare/small devices. (3) Dishwasher fires on everything (P=0.005) - no OFF suppression mechanism in the watts path.

Discarded: min_device_f1 tie 0 -> 0. Next hypothesis (EXP-05): head-role separation - route detection through the ON head: train power head with MSE masked to device-ON positions only (amplitude where it matters; Adam handles the small fridge targets), keep class-balanced BCE for the ON head, predict watts = max_w * core_power * gate(sigmoid(on_logit) > per-device gate threshold calibrated on calib ON/OFF sigmoid quantiles). Diagnostics: per-device gate ON-p05 vs OFF-p95 separation on calib.
title: EXP-04: output-scale calib inert; dead heads measured at 0W
summary: Calib least-squares scales all ~1.0 (dead heads have no signal to scale). New diagnostics: microwave/fridge/washing_machine pred p95 ON = 0W vs true 1588/90/1778W. min_device_f1 still 0.

asi.hypothesis: Per-device least-squares output-scale calibration from calib sessions fixes the level mismatch without weight drift.
asi.rollback_reason: Scales all ~1.0 - dead heads (pred exactly 0W on calib ON positions) have no signal to rescale. Calibration fixes live-but-miscalibrated heads only. min_device_f1 tie 0->0.
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-05 head-role separation: MSE masked to ON positions (amplitude head), BCE ON head as detector, predict watts = max_w * core * hard gate on sigmoid(on_logit) with per-device gate threshold from calib ON/OFF sigmoid quantiles. If gate separation is poor for a device, next lever: robust per-device normalization (p95 instead of nanmax) to un-starve small-amplitude gradients.

description:
v5 head-role separation (on top of the stability recipe; no fine-tune, no output-scale): (1) power head output = softplus (clamp(min=0) was a dead-ReLU trap - zero gradient once a channel's pre-activation goes negative, consistent with microwave/fridge/washing_machine heads dying while the unclamped ON head survived on the same encoder); kept clamp(max=1.5). (2) MSE masked to device-ON positions only (power head fits amplitude where it matters; val_mse_on 0.0046 vs val_mse_full 0.144 - full-span MSE high BY DESIGN since off-segment suppression moved to the gate). (3) BCE ON head (unchanged training) now drives detection: predict watts = max_w * core * gate(sigmoid(on_logit) > gate_thr_d), gate_thr_d calibrated per device on calib sessions as midpoint(ON-p05, OFF-p95) clamped [0.05, 0.95]; plus per-device ON-median amplitude scale r_d clamped [0.5, 4].

Gate calibration diagnostics (calib = house_1 PRE-SPLIT, no eval leakage):
kettle: sigON 0.01/0.93/1.00 sigOFF 0.00/0.84 gate=0.43 r=0.89 - good separation
microwave: sigON 0.00/0.00/0.00 sigOFF 0.00/0.00 gate=0.05(floored) r=1.08 - ON head blind on calib windows
fridge: sigON 0.16/0.20/0.29 sigOFF 0.27/0.31 gate=0.23 r=0.73 - INVERTED (OFF sigmoid > ON), gate fires ~63% of eval span
washing_machine: sigON 0.55/0.96/1.00 sigOFF 0.88/0.99 gate=0.77 - severe ON/OFF overlap kills recall
dishwasher: sigON 0.00/0.00/1.00 sigOFF 0.00/0.00 gate=0.05(floored) r=0.53 - degenerate bimodal

Per-device (n_gt / n_pred / match / P / R / F1 / MAE_W / nMAE):
kettle 299 / 439 / 79 / 0.180 / 0.264 / 0.214 / 25.2 / 0.0736
microwave 262 / 73 / 3 / 0.041 / 0.011 / 0.018 / 12.6 / 0.0366
fridge 28034 / 17564 / 3325 / 0.189 / 0.119 / 0.146 / 43.2 / 0.1258
washing_machine 2966 / 651 / 13 / 0.020 / 0.004 / 0.007 / 101.0 / 0.2946
dishwasher 1353 / 1750 / 46 / 0.026 / 0.034 / 0.030 / 30.7 / 0.0894
pooled F1 0.130; coverage pred=0.666 vs true=0.258; mean_mae_w 42.53; worst 101.0 (washing_machine).

PRIMARY improved for the first time (0 -> 0.007188; min over devices, washing_machine was the binding zero). Kept per the keep-on-primary-improvement contract. Caveats logged honestly: regression got WORSE (mean_mae_w 23.60 -> 42.53) and aggregate coverage over-predicts 0.666 vs 0.258 - the gate thresholds are crude quantile midpoints on poorly separated ON heads.

Next steps (priority order): (1) per-device gate threshold by DIRECT supervised optimization on calib windows (we hold labels there - choose the threshold maximizing episode-level F1 on calib instead of quantile midpoint); (2) washing_machine ON-head separation (currently useless: ON-p05 0.55 < OFF-p95 0.99) and amplitude (r hit the 1.58 clamp, MAE 101); (3) fridge gate firing discipline (inverted sigmoid). Expanded eval (BENCH_EVAL=90d/full) scheduled as verification once the next mechanism-level change lands - guarding against overfitting the 30-day eval window.
title: EXP-05: head-role separation revives all 5 device heads
summary: Softplus power head + MSE-on-ON + BCE-detector gate with calib thresholds: min_device_f1 0->0.0072 (first >0), pooled F1 0.001->0.130, all devices firing. Tradeoff: MAE 23.6->42.5, coverage over-predicts 0.67 vs 0.26.

asi.hypothesis: Head-role separation (softplus power head + MSE-on-ON amplitude + BCE-detector gate with calib-calibrated thresholds) revives the dead heads and lifts min_device_f1 above zero for the first time.
asi.next_action_hint: Gate threshold by direct supervised episode-F1 optimization on calib windows (replaces quantile midpoint); then washing_machine ON-head separation + amplitude (r clamped at 1.58, MAE 101) and fridge gate discipline (inverted sigmoid). Run expanded eval (90d) as overfit check when the next mechanism change lands.

description:
EXP-06 v6 = v5 + head-only ON-head calibration fine-tune (freeze encoder+power head; FT head_on ~2.3k params on 25 calib windows, per-device masked BCE, LR 1e-3, 60 epochs; gates re-derived from FT-ed head).

MOTIVATION (source-channel audit + pre-FT source-val diagnostics): microwave ON head blind (sig ON p50 0.0), fridge NO separation even in-domain (ON p50 0.49 vs OFF p50 0.49), dishwasher ON/OFF overlap (0.99 vs 0.28), wm overlap (0.25/0.99 vs 0.02/0.63) - while kettle transferred (ON 1.0 vs OFF 0.0). Audit also KILLED two planned ideas with evidence: predict-side duration filter (wm/fridge ON labels are 2-sample-blip dominated in ALL houses: run_p50=2 samples, house_2 wm p50_on_w=272W, house_5=498W, house_1-pre=245W -> GT episodes are short; a duration filter would destroy recall) and calib threshold sweep (calib windows are session-centered/ON-heavy, sweep inherits that bias).

RESULT: catastrophic secondary collapse. Post-FT source-val sigmoid saturates - fridge/wm/dishwasher OFF p50 = 1.0/1.0/1.0 (pre-FT: 0.49/0.02/0.28); calib_bce 12.47 -> 0.55 (memorization regime). Gates recalibrated to kettle 0.88 / microwave 0.86 / fridge 0.85 / wm 0.95 / dishwasher 0.85 (v5: 0.43/0.05/0.23/0.77/0.05).

Per-device (v6 vs v5): kettle F1 0.150 vs 0.214, MAE 30.4 vs 25.2; microwave F1 0.096 vs 0.018, MAE 60.3 vs 12.6 (THE one genuine gain: R 0.237, 62/1032 - head FT did repair microwave); fridge F1 0.018 vs 0.146, MAE 58.7 vs 43.2 (R 0.119 -> 0.010, preds 17564 -> 2488 at gate 0.85); washing_machine F1 0.008 vs 0.007, MAE 105.0 vs 101.0 (matches 14 vs 13 - the entire nominal primary improvement is +1 episode); dishwasher F1 0.015 vs 0.030, MAE 120.9 vs 30.7 (preds exploded 1750 -> 12404, P 0.008). nMAE: kettle 0.089, microwave 0.176, fridge 0.171, wm 0.306, dishwasher 0.353.

Aggregates (v6 vs v5): min_device_f1 0.008065 vs 0.007188; mean_device_f1 0.0575 vs 0.0829; pooled_episode_f1 0.0208 vs 0.1298 (-84%); mean_mae_w 75.07 vs 42.53 (+76%); worst_mae_w 120.9 vs 101.0; mean_nmae 0.2189 vs 0.1240; coverage_pred 1.2026 vs 0.6664 (predicts MORE watts than the aggregate - physically impossible); coverage_true 0.2582 (unchanged).

WHY DISCARD DESPITE PRIMARY NOMINALLY IMPROVING: +0.0009 min_device_f1 = one extra matched wm episode (13 -> 14 of 2966) - statistical noise; every tracked secondary regressed. Keeping would overfit the single primary number and enshrine a strictly worse model (user constraint: do not overfit to the benchmarks). Mechanism not invalidated - execution was.

ROOT CAUSE: calib FT reused PRETRAIN pos_weight (wm/microwave capped 50 for source rarity) on CALIB positions where fridge is 76% ON / wm 72% ON / dishwasher 84% ON -> head pushed toward constant-ON -> sigmoid saturation; 60 epochs x LR 1e-3 on 25 windows amplified it; gate recalibration then amplified the saturated head's damage.

GUARDS HONORED: calib = target-house pre-split sessions only; power head frozen during FT (val_mse_full 0.14412 at pretrain end == post-FT by construction); 30d min_device_f1 unchanged as decision metric; no eval-span-derived parameters anywhere; no duration filter / threshold sweep shipped (audit-refuted).

NEXT (EXP-07): re-run head-only FT correctly - per-device pos_weight computed on CALIB positions (kettle ~5.3, microwave ~10.1, fridge/wm/dishwasher -> 1.0), LR 3e-4, <=15 epochs, weight decay, early-stop saturation guard (any device source-val OFF-sig p50 > 0.5 -> stop); recycle microwave mechanism; keep v5 gates for kettle if its calibration degrades.
title: v6 head-only ON FT saturates; pooled F1 collapses
summary: Head-only ON FT saturated: source-val sig OFF p50=1.0, gates 0.85-0.95, fridge R 0.010, MAE 75.1W, cov 1.20x. min_f1 +0.0009 = 1 extra match (noise). Discard.

asi.hypothesis: Head-only ON-head calibration fine-tune (freeze encoder+power head) repairs the three ON heads that are uncorrelated with house_1 truth without the v3 whole-net drift
asi.rollback_reason: Primary gain is noise-level (+1 matched wm episode); pooled F1 -84%, MAE +76%, coverage 1.20x of aggregate; FT saturated (source-val sig OFF p50 1.0) because pretrain pos_weight (up to 50) was applied to ON-heavy calib positions
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-07: same head-only FT but per-device pos_weight from CALIB positions (kettle 5.3, microwave 10.1, others 1.0), LR 3e-4, <=15 epochs, weight decay, early-stop when any source-val OFF-sig p50 > 0.5; microwave repair (F1 0.018->0.096) is real and worth recycling

description:
EXP-07 v7 = v5 + GUARDED head-only ON FT (the v6 fixes applied): per-device pos_weight from CALIB positions (kettle 4.7, microwave 8.8, fridge/wm/dishwasher 1.0 - vs v6's pretrain pos_weight up to 50), AdamW LR 3e-4 + weight decay 1e-4, saturation guard = trip when head weight norm > 2.5x init OR any device's calib OFF-sigmoid p50 rises > 0.15 over its pre-FT base; restore last-passing snapshot; pre-FT head = safe fallback.

GUARD BEHAVIOR: init head norm 1.72, cap 4.30; calib OFF p50 base [0.0, 0.0, 0.27, 0.88, 0.0]; calib_bce epoch 0 = 3.18 (v6 started at 12.47 - the pos_weight fix worked); TRIP at ft epoch 7 on fridge off-p50 (0.42 > cap 0.42); snapshot from epoch ~6 restored (norm 1.71). Guard fired correctly - no v6-style saturation (post-FT source-val OFF p50: kettle 0.0, microwave 0.01, fridge 0.75, wm 0.01, dishwasher 0.51 - vs v6's all-1.0).

RESULT vs v5: min_device_f1 0.006154 vs 0.007188 (REGRESSED - decision metric); mean_device_f1 0.0694 vs 0.0829; pooled_episode_f1 0.0723 vs 0.1298; mean_mae_w 44.94 vs 42.53; worst_mae_w 94.79 vs 101.04 (best so far); mean_nmae 0.1310 vs 0.1240; coverage_pred 0.702 vs 0.666.

Per-device (v7 vs v5): kettle F1 0.183 vs 0.214, MAE 29.3 vs 25.2 (gate 0.43->0.47); microwave F1 0.054 vs 0.018, MAE 20.3 vs 12.6 (SECOND independent confirmation: head FT reliably repairs microwave - 15 matches vs 3, 298 preds vs 73; though the post-FT head is calib-blind sig 0/0/0, eval improved anyway); fridge F1 0.081 vs 0.146, MAE 44.0 vs 43.2 (THE regression: FT raised fridge calib OFF p50 0.27->0.40 (still inverted sigOFF>sigON) -> gate 0.23->0.36 -> R 0.119->0.060, matches 3325->1680); washing_machine F1 0.006 vs 0.007 (gate 0.76, unchanged pathology); dishwasher F1 0.023 vs 0.030 (matches 51 vs 44 but preds 3063 vs 1750).

WHY DISCARD: primary regressed; the guard contained saturation but could not contain CALIBRATION DRIFT - 7 full-batch steps at LR 3e-4 sufficed to move the fridge head's OFF distribution +0.13, and the midpoint gate rule amplified that into a 2x recall loss. Net reshuffle: microwave +0.036 vs fridge -0.065.

MECHANISM INSIGHT (carries to EXP-08): the gates are hyper-sensitive to head changes because they are derived from the head's own calib quantiles; any head repair necessarily moves those quantiles. Changed assumption for retry: anchor the FT-ed head to its PRE-FT source-val sigmoid outputs (distillation-style consistency term L = BCE_calib + lambda * MSE(sig_ft(x_val), sig_pre(x_val)), lambda ~ 5, anchor subset ~2000 val windows) so the head nudge is calibration-preserving - v6 failed via saturation, v7 failed via drift; the anchor targets exactly that degree of freedom. Microwave's cross-run-consistent gain (0.018 -> 0.054-0.096) is the prize worth anchoring for.

GUARDS HONORED: calib = target-house pre-split sessions only; power head frozen (val_mse_full 0.14412 pre == post by construction); no eval-derived parameters; audit-refuted ideas (duration filter, calib threshold sweep) still not shipped.
title: v7 guarded head FT: drift moves gates, fridge recall halves
summary: Guard tripped at ft epoch 7 (fridge off-p50); snapshot restore kept drift that pushed gate 0.23->0.36, fridge F1 0.146->0.081. min_f1 0.0062 < v5 0.0072. Discard.

asi.hypothesis: Guarded head-only ON FT (calib pos_weight, LR 3e-4+wd, norm/off-p50 tripwires) repairs ON heads without v6 saturation
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.007188->0.006154; guard contained saturation but 7 steps of calibration drift moved fridge gate 0.23->0.36 and halved fridge recall; gate rule amplifies any head change
asi.next_action_hint: EXP-08: anchor-FT - L = BCE_calib + 5*MSE(sig_ft(x_val_anchor), sig_pre(x_val_anchor)) on ~2000 source-val windows so head repair is calibration-preserving; keep gate rule; microwave gain is cross-run consistent (0.018->0.054 in v7, ->0.096 in v6)

description:
EXP-08 v8 = v5 + ANCHORED head-only ON FT: kept v7's guard set (calib pos_weight kettle 4.7/microwave 8.8/rest 1.0, AdamW LR 3e-4 wd 1e-4, norm 2.5x + off-p50 +0.15 tripwires, snapshot restore) and added distillation anchor L_ft = BCE_calib + 5.0 * MSE(sig_ft(x_anchor), sig_pre(x_anchor)), x_anchor = 2000 source-val windows, sig_pre = frozen pre-FT sigmoids.

ANCHOR RESULT: anchor_mse stayed 0.0004 (epoch 0) - the source-val sigmoid map barely moved - YET the fridge calib off-p50 still rose 0.27 -> 0.45 (trip at ft epoch 6, same tripwire as v7) and the restored snapshot still moved the fridge gate 0.23 -> 0.38. MECHANISM (closes the head-FT family): the anchor pins the head on SOURCE-house inputs, but calib windows are TARGET-house (house_1) inputs - out-of-distribution for the anchor - and the gates are derived from exactly those target-house calib quantiles. No source-side regularizer can pin target-house head behavior; only target-house labels could, and we have just 25 windows of them (v3's whole-net FT showed they overfit when used aggressively).

RESULT vs v5: min_device_f1 0.008436 vs 0.007188 (nominal best so far); mean_device_f1 0.0623 vs 0.0829; pooled_episode_f1 0.0518 vs 0.1298 (-60%); mean_mae_w 45.23 vs 42.53; worst_mae_w 93.47 vs 101.04 (best so far); mean_nmae 0.1319 vs 0.1240; coverage_pred 0.707 vs 0.666.

Per-device (v8 vs v5): kettle F1 0.175 vs 0.214 (gate 0.43->0.48); microwave F1 0.050 vs 0.018 (3rd confirmation of the repair, but anchor dampened it: v6 0.096, v7 0.054, v8 0.050); fridge F1 0.057 vs 0.146 (gate 0.23->0.38, R 0.042, matches 1182 vs 3325); washing_machine F1 0.008 vs 0.007 (15 vs 13 matches - the entire nominal primary gain is +2 episodes); dishwasher F1 0.021 vs 0.030 (preds 4193 vs 1750). nMAE: kettle 0.087, microwave 0.060, fridge 0.129, wm 0.273, dishwasher 0.111.

WHY DISCARD DESPITE NOMINAL PRIMARY GAIN: +0.00125 = 2 extra matched wm episodes of 2966 (noise); pooled F1 -60%, mean_device_f1 -25%. Third consecutive head-FT variant (v6 unguarded, v7 guarded, v8 anchored) redistributes F1 across devices while pooled F1 always drops and the primary wiggles at noise level. Family closed on mechanism: calib supervision (25 house_1 windows) is too weak to repair heads without breaking others, and the gate rule amplifies every head change. Keeping would enshrine a holistically worse model - exactly the benchmark-overfitting the task forbids.

GUARDS HONORED: calib = target-house pre-split only; anchor = source-val only (no target leakage); power head frozen (val_mse_full 0.14412 unchanged by construction); no eval-derived parameters; audit-refuted ideas (duration filter, threshold sweep) still not shipped.

NEXT (EXP-09): pivot away from head modification entirely. Diagnose the wm bottleneck structurally first (wm is the min device: F1 0.007, R 0.004, matches 13/2966 ~= chance-level onset alignment) - inspect the eval GT wm episode-duration structure (diagnostic only, no parameters from it) vs the source audit's 2-sample-blip domination (house_1-pre wm run_p50 = 2 samples, 34390 runs); then choose between (a) mechanisms that help ALL devices (i3 longer pretrain, i10 energy-balance) and (b) documenting a structural cap if wm GT is ~undetectable blip noise. No more head-FT retries without a genuinely new assumption.

description:
EXP-09 v9 = v5 with i3 (longer source fit): EPOCHS 12 -> 24, N_TRAIN_WINDOWS 40000 -> 80000. Everything else identical (same seed, LR, pos_weight cap 50, gates, calibration). No eval-derived parameters.

TRAINING EVIDENCE: BCE kept descending 27.7 (e0) -> 5.97 (e23), ~2.4x lower than v5's end (8.38); val_mse_on fluctuates 0.003-0.006 (plateau region), val_mse_full noisy 0.13-0.19. So the source fit DID improve - the hypothesis was that better fit lifts all heads.

RESULT vs v5: min_device_f1 0.007565 vs 0.007188 (nominal +5.3%); mean_device_f1 0.0804 vs 0.0829; pooled_episode_f1 0.0414 vs 0.1298 (-68%); mean_mae_w 54.45 vs 42.53 (+28%); worst_mae_w 119.18 vs 101.04; mean_nmae 0.1588 vs 0.1240; coverage_pred 0.882 vs 0.666 (now OVER-predicts energy by 3.4x of aggregate share).

Per-device (v9 vs v5): kettle F1 0.320 vs 0.214, MAE 16.8 vs 25.2, matches 90 vs 71 (P 0.342, R 0.301) - GENUINE improvement, consistent with kettle being the best-transferring head (channel audit: kettle signature matches across houses). microwave F1 0.017 vs 0.018 (MAE 10.7 improved). fridge F1 0.042 vs 0.146, matches 798 vs 3325. washing_machine F1 0.008 vs 0.007, matches 13 vs 13 (IDENTICAL match count). dishwasher F1 0.015 vs 0.030, MAE 119.2 vs 30.7.

WHY DISCARD: the primary gain is wm F1 arithmetic from FEWER predictions (651 -> 471 episodes, same 13 matches -> P 0.020 -> 0.028), not mechanism. Meanwhile pooled F1 -68%, MAE +28%, coverage 3.4x over. i3 hypothesis (better source fit lifts all heads) is REFUTED at 2x scale: 3 of 5 devices got worse.

MECHANISM (why more training hurt): the pos_weight-capped BCE (up to 50) pushes rare-device ON-heads toward constant-ON with more optimization - calib diagnostics show wm head SATURATED (sigON p50 1.00, sigOFF p50 0.98, gate 0.95 vs v5's 0.77) and fridge separation collapsed (sigON p50 0.13, gate 0.18). The dishwasher POWER head nearly died (calib ON median 16 W vs v5's 228 W) - consistent with the channel audit: house_2 dishwasher 1984 W vs house_5 97 W signatures teach contradictory amplitude, and 2x more epochs amplify the conflict. GENUINE SIGNAL to keep in the design memory: kettle (well-separated, cross-house-consistent) benefits strongly from longer fit - future mechanisms that manage the fit-saturation tradeoff (weight averaging, per-head capacity, loss reshaping) could capture kettle's gain without the saturation damage.

GUARDS HONORED: calib = target-house pre-split only; source val untouched for training; no eval-derived parameters.

NEXT: user directed backlog expansion from docs/research/analog-problems.md + transfer-applicability-audit.md before next mechanism pick.

description:
EXP-10 v10 = v5 net (training identical, same seed) + factorial-HMM Viterbi decode in predict (research import: analog-problems.md S2.1 factorial HMM, S2.3 dwell priors, S4 step 4; user-directed backlog i15+i16). Per-sample gating replaced by: per-position mean posterior (same overlap scheme), logit shift by the SAME calib gate (v5 decision boundary preserved), exact joint Viterbi over 2^5=32 states with factorized transitions; emissions = per-chain log-liks + soft sum-to-aggregate Gaussian (sigma = 497 W, aggregate-minus-devices residual std on SOURCE houses); transitions = geometric dwell priors from SOURCE-house run-length MEANS; amplitudes = calib ON medians floored at 1.2x thr (kettle 2331, microwave 1588, fridge 90, wm 1778, dishwasher 122 W). All priors from source train split + calib only; eval span used only at inference.

RESULT vs v5: min_device_f1 0.000000 vs 0.007188 (COLLAPSE - fridge and dishwasher both exactly 0); mean_device_f1 0.0629 vs 0.0829; pooled_episode_f1 0.0066 vs 0.1298; BUT mean_mae_w 29.48 vs 42.53 (-31%, best yet); worst_mae_w 62.59 vs 101.04 (best yet); mean_nmae 0.0860 vs 0.1240 (best yet); coverage_pred 0.437 vs 0.666 (true 0.258 - best energy accounting yet).

Per-device (v10 vs v5): kettle F1 0.283 vs 0.214 (P 0.383 vs 0.162 - precision DOUBLED, matches 67, preds 175 vs 439), MAE 13.2 vs 25.2; microwave F1 0.007 vs 0.018 (32 preds, 1 match); fridge F1 0.000 vs 0.146 (185 preds, 0 matches); washing_machine F1 0.025 vs 0.007 (matches 44 vs 13, P 0.079, R 0.015 - 3.5x, decode's first real min-device-relevant gain); dishwasher F1 0.000 vs 0.030 (214 preds, 0 matches).

MECHANISM DIAGNOSIS (why 0s): the dwell prior was fit on SOURCE-house run-length MEANS: E_on fridge 35.1, dishwasher 25.4, kettle 21.1, microwave 12.0, wm 4.5 samples. Predicted episodes are therefore ~2.5-3.5 min for fridge/dw, but the EXP-08 GT diagnostic showed eval GT episodes are blip-dominated (fridge p50 30 s = 5 samples, 83% <= 36 s; dw p50 30 s): duration ratio ~7 > the frozen band [1/3, 3] -> EVERY episode rejected. Root cause: heavy-tailed run-length distributions - the MEAN is set by rare long cycles while the GT-matching structure is the MEDIAN (house_1-pre audit: fridge run_p50 5 samples, wm 2). The geometric mean-fit is the wrong robust statistic, not a wrong mechanism: kettle (whose source mean happens to be closer to its GT median) and wm (E_on 4.5 ~= GT 4) improved exactly as the mechanism predicts.

WHAT IS GENUINE AND KEEPABLE IN DESIGN MEMORY: (1) joint decoding + aggregate consistency produces the best energy accounting of any run (coverage 0.437 vs true 0.258; MAE -31%) - the sum constraint works; (2) precision improved where posteriors are good (kettle P 0.383 - the decoder suppresses v5's spurious flicker episodes 439 -> 175); (3) wm's first mechanism-level gain (13 -> 44 matches). The failure is ONE parameter: the location statistic of the dwell fit.

NEXT (EXP-11, single knob): median-based dwell statistic - pool SOURCE-house run lengths per device, p_cont = 1 - 2^(-1/median) (median-matched geometric), fallbacks unchanged. Predicted episode lengths then track the blip-dominated GT structure (~2-6 samples) instead of the tail. No other changes.

description:
EXP-11 v11 = v10's factorial-HMM Viterbi decode with ONE knob changed: the per-chain geometric dwell prior fit on pooled SOURCE-house run-length MEDIANS (p_cont = 1 - 2^(-1/median)) instead of means. Net/training identical to v5 (same seed, same pretrain curves). Priors: sigma 497 W; amps kettle 2331/microwave 1588/fridge 90/wm 1778/dw 122 W; med_on kettle 23.0/microwave 9.0/fridge 29.0/wm 2.0/dishwasher 14.0 samples; med_off 29-35. All from source train split + calib; eval span inference-only.

RESULT vs v5: min_device_f1 0.002147 vs 0.007188 (regressed - min device switched from wm to dishwasher); mean_device_f1 0.1501 vs 0.0829 (+81%, best yet); pooled_episode_f1 0.1216 vs 0.1298 (-6%); mean_mae_w 29.26 vs 42.53 (-31%, best yet); worst_mae_w 62.62 vs 101.04 (best yet); mean_nmae 0.0853 vs 0.1240 (-31%, best yet); coverage_pred 0.437 vs 0.666 (true 0.258).

Per-device (v11 vs v5): washing_machine F1 0.335 vs 0.007 (matches 806 vs 13, P 0.435, R 0.272 - the decode's headline: the wm head's "blindness" was a GATING artifact, not posterior absence; short dwell + aggregate consistency aligns its firing with the aggregate 866 W wm signature); kettle F1 0.302 vs 0.214 (P 0.348, R 0.268, MAE 14.5); fridge F1 0.094 vs 0.146 (P 0.412 vs 0.189 - precision 2.2x - but R 0.053 vs 0.119: 3623 preds of ~29-40 samples vs GT p50 5-sample fragments; recall still capped by cross-house dwell mismatch); microwave F1 0.017 ~ 0.018; dishwasher F1 0.002 vs 0.030 (510 preds, 2 matches: source med_on 14 samples vs house_1 dw GT ~5 samples, and the dw posterior fires at wrong times - v5's dw "F1 0.030" was 44 lucky matches from threshold-0.05 flicker, itself near-noise).

WHY DISCARD: the frozen primary (30d min_device_f1) regressed 0.0072 -> 0.0021. Per the task's standing rule (keep only on genuine primary improvement; ties discard), a mechanism that improves 4/5 devices and every regression metric but lowers the min-device primary is still a discard. The decision-metric choice itself (min vs mean) is the user's to revisit - flagged, not acted on.

DESIGN MEMORY (the decode family is now the strongest mechanism found): (1) joint decode + sum constraint = best energy accounting of all 11 runs (MAE -31%, coverage 0.437); (2) duration alignment via median dwell turned wm from worst device (0.007) to best (0.335); (3) remaining bottleneck = cross-house dwell-structure mismatch: SOURCE medians (fridge 29, dw 14) reflect source houses' threshold-relative channel structure, while house_1's channels fragment differently (audit: house_1-pre fridge run_p50 5, dw ~5) - the prior transfers only where structures match (wm: 2 vs 4 OK).

NEXT (EXP-12, single knob): calib-corrected dwell prior - measure complete (edge-truncation-free) run lengths inside the 5 calib windows per device (house_1 PRE-split, the SAME sanctioned data budget as gates/amps); when >= 8 complete runs observed, use the calib median for that device's dwell prior, else keep the source median. Expect fridge/dw medians to drop toward house_1's ~5-sample structure, lifting fridge recall and dw F1. No eval-span data, no new data budget.

description:
EXP-12 v12 = v11 + calib-corrected ON dwell prior (complete edge-truncation-free run medians inside the 5 calib windows per device, >= 8 runs threshold; else source median). Implementation note: first attempt crashed (ctx['calib'][dev] is a DICT {'mains_win','device_win'} with a session axis, not a list of sessions - fixed to iterate the session axis; crash cost one failed bench, no log entry).

RESULT: bit-identical to v11 on every metric (min_device_f1 0.002147, mean 0.150116, pooled 0.121577, MAE 29.2581 - all 6 decimals equal). Reason discovered post-hoc: calib medians came out kettle 8.5/microwave 2.0/fridge 4.0/wm 4.0/dishwasher 5.0 samples (all >= 8 complete runs, all USED), but p_cont = 1 - 2^(-1/median) gives 0.078/0.293/0.159/0.159/0.129 - ALL below the VP_PCONT_MIN = 0.5 clamp -> every ON-side transition = log(0.5), exactly as in v11 (source medians 23/9/29/2/14 -> 0.030/0.074/0.024/0.293/0.048, also all clamped). The entire dwell-prior mechanism has been INERT since v11; the Viterbi degenerated to a per-position joint MAP over emissions.

ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION (run 11 log overstated the dwell prior): v11's wm 47x / kettle +41% / precision gains came from the EMISSION design - logit-shifted posteriors (v5 decision boundary preserved) + soft sum-to-aggregate consistency + per-state constant amplitudes - with UNIFORM transitions. The v10->v11 change that mattered was UNDOING v10's sticky ON transitions (source mean-fit p_cont 0.97 -> clamped 0.5), not the median statistic per se. The dwell mechanism remains UNTESTED in its operative form.

CALIB DIAGNOSTIC GOLD (calib-only evidence, for the amplitude decision): calib ON-watt p25/p50/p75/p90 - kettle 2302/2331/2361/2392 (tight); microwave 1571/1588/1602/1613 (tight); fridge 88/90/91/95 (tight); washing_machine 339/1778/1957/2004 (low-power mode at p25); DISHWASHER 121/122/2331/2360 - STRONGLY BIMODAL: the calib dw sessions caught both a ~122 W mode and a ~2360 W heating mode. The decode's dw amplitude (calib median 122 W) represents the low mode, so the aggregate constraint barely notices dw ON (122 W << sigma 497 W) - dw states are physics-unconstrained and its blind posterior fires 510 misaligned episodes (P 0.004). This is the concrete mechanism behind dw = min-device at 0.002.

WHY DISCARD: primary unchanged from v11 (0.002147 < v5 0.0072); the intended knob never activated; the run's value is the clamp discovery + the dw amplitude diagnosis, not the metric.

NEXT (EXP-13, single knob): make the dwell prior OPERATIVE - switch the parameterization to the geometric mean-matched form p_cont = 1 - 1/median (mean run length = calib median: kettle 8.5 -> p 0.882, dw 5 -> 0.8, fridge 4 -> 0.75, wm 4 -> 0.75, microwave 2 -> 0.5, OFF ~33 -> 0.97), all >= the 0.5 floor so nothing is clamped. Emissions unchanged -> clean A/B: any delta is purely temporal coupling. Watch: sticky OFF (entry cost -3.4 nats vs -0.69) may suppress weak microwave/dw firing; if so v14 isolates the OFF side back to 0.5. Also queued (v14+, calib-evidence-backed): dw amplitude from the calib ON p75 (2331 W heating mode) instead of the median (122 W) - one device, one statistic, calib-only.

description:
EXP-13 v13 = v11/v12 decode with the dwell prior made OPERATIVE: p_cont = 1 - 1/median (geometric mean run length = median) on CALIB complete-run medians (all 5 devices used calib; on_p_cont kettle 0.882/fridge 0.75/wm 0.75/dishwasher 0.8/microwave 0.5) and SOURCE OFF medians (off_p_cont ~0.97). Emissions identical to v11/v12 -> clean A/B on temporal coupling alone.

RESULT vs v11 (uniform transitions): min_device_f1 0.000000 vs 0.002147 (fridge AND dishwasher exactly 0 again); mean_device_f1 0.0649 vs 0.1501; pooled_episode_f1 0.0074 vs 0.1216; mean_mae_w 29.41 (unchanged - energy accounting insensitive to decode coupling); coverage_pred 0.387 vs 0.437.

Per-device (v13 vs v11): kettle F1 0.285 vs 0.302 (178 preds vs 230); microwave 0.007 vs 0.017 (34 preds vs 88 - the predicted OFF-stickiness suppression of weak firing, exactly as flagged in the v13 docstring risk); fridge 0.000 vs 0.094 (252 preds of long episodes vs 3623 short - sticky ON re-extends the inverted fridge head's runs past the duration band, v10's failure mode); washing_machine 0.033 vs 0.335 (589 vs 1853 preds - wm's 806 matches came from FREQUENT SHORT episodes, which stickiness destroys); dishwasher 0.000 vs 0.002 (221 vs 510).

MECHANISM CONCLUSION (3-regime comparison, now closed): (a) v10 sticky-ON source-mean (p 0.97): fridge/dw 0, pooled 0.0066; (b) v11/v12 UNIFORM (all p_cont clamped to 0.5 -> per-position joint MAP): fridge 0.094, wm 0.335, pooled 0.1216 - BEST; (c) v13 operative both-sided: fridge/dw 0, pooled 0.0074. The gate-shifted posterior + aggregate-consistency emissions fire in GT-like blips on their own; ANY temporal stickiness lengthens episodes beyond the frozen duration band [1/3, 3]. The dwell/kinetics prior idea (analog-problems S2.3, backlog i16) is REFUTED for this benchmark in both directions; the factorial joint MAP (i15) is VALIDATED as the vehicle. Do not revive dwell priors without a changed emission scale (e.g., unclamped posteriors would rebalance entry/exit costs).

WHY DISCARD: primary collapsed to 0. The run's value is closing the dwell-prior question with a clean single-knob A/B.

NEXT (EXP-14, single knob on the WINNING configuration): v14 = v11/v12 uniform-transition decode + DISHWASHER AMPLITUDE FIX - amp statistic for all devices = calib ON-watt p75 instead of median (calib-only evidence from run 12's diagnostic: dw calib ON watts are BIMODAL 121/122/2331/2360 - the median 122 W is the low mode, leaving dw states physics-unconstrained by the aggregate penalty (122 W << sigma 497 W) and its blind posterior fires 510 misaligned episodes; p75 = 2331 W forces dw episodes to align with ~2.3 kW aggregate steps). Tight devices barely move (kettle 2361, microwave 1602, fridge 91); wm 1778->1957. Expected: dw P rises sharply; watch dw MAE (episodes now carry 2331 W - wrong-time firing is 19x more expensive) and the kettle/dw state aliasing (both amps ~2331 - only posteriors can separate them).

description:
EXP-14 v14 = v11/v12 uniform-transition joint MAP (constant logA, verified identical regime) + amplitude statistic changed from calib ON median to calib ON P75 (VP_AMP_PCT 75). Amps: kettle 2361, microwave 1602, fridge 91, washing_machine 1957, dishwasher 2331 (was 2331/1588/90/1778/122). Calib-only evidence base (run 12 diagnostic): dw calib ON watts bimodal 121/122/2331/2360.

RESULT vs v11: min_device_f1 0.000000 vs 0.002147 (microwave joined dishwasher at exactly 0); mean_device_f1 0.157419 vs 0.150116 (+4.9%, best yet); pooled_episode_f1 0.123076 vs 0.121576 (+1.2%); mean_mae_w 29.89 vs 29.26; worst_mae_w 68.03 vs 62.62 (wm amp +179 W raises wrong-time cost); coverage_pred 0.449 vs 0.437.

Per-device (v14 vs v11): KETTLE F1 0.354 vs 0.302 (+17%) - P 0.537 vs 0.348 (best precision of the loop), preds 147 vs 230, matches 79, MAE 6.7 W vs 14.5 (HALVED - best device-level regression ever; the tight calib distribution + aggregate constraint = near-oracle kettle); fridge 0.095 vs 0.094 (unchanged, P 0.415); washing_machine 0.338 vs 0.335 (800 matches, stable); MICROWAVE 0.000 vs 0.017 (5 preds vs 88 - its ~1.6-2.0 kW draws are now better explained by the wm state (amp 1957): the aggregate term reassigns them; the mw head adds nothing unique); DISHWASHER 0.000 vs 0.002 (209 preds vs 510, 0 matches - forcing aggregate consistency onto the blind dw posterior produces ZERO aligned episodes: its spikes anti-correlate with ~2.3 kW aggregate steps. The 'constrain a blind posterior with physics' hypothesis is REFUTED for dw).

MECHANISM CONCLUSIONS: (1) the aggregate-consistency penalty + accurate amplitude is a powerful ORACLE for heads with informative posteriors (kettle: P 0.537, MAE 6.7 W) and a destructive re-assigner for blind ones (mw/dw); (2) dw cannot be fixed on the decode side - its posterior timing is uninformative on the target house; posterior repair must come from target-distribution training data; (3) amp statistic per se: p75 helps tight devices (kettle), hurts via cross-state reassignment (mw).

WHY DISCARD: primary 0.000 < v5 0.0072. The kettle/aggregate discovery is design memory.

NEXT (EXP-15, new mechanism family - i19/audit route 7 source-free adaptation, PROMOTED): repair the blind dw/mw posteriors with self-training on the PRE-SPLIT target aggregate (legal: same split as calib, no eval span): run the v11-config decode on house_1 PRE-split mains, take high-confidence joint states as pseudo-labels (confidence = emission margin), fine-tune ONLY the head layers at low LR for a few steps with the pseudo-labels, then re-derive gates/amps from calib as usual and decode eval. description:
EXP-15 v15 = visibility-routed hybrid decode (i15 continuation). Mechanism: route each chain by AGGREGATE VISIBILITY = calib ON-median amplitude / aggregate-residual sigma (sigma 497 W from source-train mains minus all 5 device channels). vis >= 1 (kettle 4.69, microwave 3.20, washing_machine 3.58) -> exact additive-factorial joint MAP over 2^3 = 8 states (emissions = per-chain logit-shifted posterior log-liks, shift by the SAME calib gate; + soft sum-to-aggregate Gaussian; uniform constant logA). vis < 1 (fridge 0.18, dishwasher 0.25) -> keep the v5 per-sample power x gate path verbatim. Justification (runs 10-14 evidence): the sum-to-aggregate term only carries information when the chain's amplitude is resolvable above the noise floor; below that it is posterior-only and measured WORSE than v5's direct detector (run 14: constraining blind dw = 0/209 aligned episodes; decode fridge 0.094 vs v5 0.146). The routing gap is 13x (3.20 vs 0.25) - robust to any threshold in [0.3, 3.0]; all inputs calib/source-derived.

RESULT vs v5 (mainline) and v11 (best decode-only): min_device_f1 0.010152 vs 0.007188 (+41%) and vs 0.002147; mean_device_f1 0.156883 vs 0.082936 (+89%) and vs 0.150116; pooled_episode_f1 0.154406 vs 0.129835 (+19%) and vs 0.121576 (best pooled of the loop); mean_mae_w 34.29 vs 42.53 (-19%) and vs 29.26 (worse than v11 - direct fridge/dw flicker costs MAE); worst_mae_w 67.70 vs 101.04 (-33%); mean_nmae 0.09997 vs 0.12402 (-19%); coverage_pred 0.533 vs 0.666 (true 0.258).

Per-device (v15 | v5 | v11): KETTLE F1 0.286 | 0.214 | 0.302 - matches 82, preds 275 (8-state MAP fires a bit differently than v11's 32-state: P 0.298 vs 0.348); MICROWAVE 0.010 | 0.018 | 0.017 - 132 preds 2 matches: HONEST REGRESSION, mw is the new min device (its posterior is blind; vis 3.20 put it in the MAP where it underperforms v5 flicker - noted, not tuned); FRIDGE 0.146 | 0.146 | 0.094 - bit-exact v5 reproduction as designed (17564 preds, 3325 matches, MAE 43.2); WASHING_MACHINE 0.313 | 0.007 | 0.335 - 749 matches (58x v5's 13), P 0.412, MAE 67.7; DISHWASHER 0.030 | 0.030 | 0.002 - bit-exact v5 (1750 preds, 46 matches, MAE 30.7).

WHY KEEP: genuine primary improvement (+41%) carried by an unambiguous mechanism (wm 13 -> 749 matches), every secondary at-or-better than v5, routing is calib/source-derived with a 13x separation gap, and the fallback devices add no new freedom (exact v5 reproduction). No eval-derived parameters anywhere.

ANTI-OVERFIT STATEMENT: no eval-span GT statistics entered the design; the routing rule and all amplitudes/sigma/gates come from calib sessions and source houses only; the fridge/dw paths are frozen v5 behavior (same seed, same calib -> identical outputs), so the only new freedom is the MAP over the three high-vis chains. Expanded-eval check (BENCH_EVAL=90d) remains mandatory before calling this final.

NEXT: the min device is now microwave (0.010, vis 3.20 but blind posterior - the MAP underuses it). Candidates: (a) calib-only routing refinement - route by visibility AND calib posterior separability (mw calib sigON p95 0.00 = no separable signal), which would move mw to the direct path WITHOUT any eval evidence; (b) i19 self-training on pre-split aggregate for the blind heads, now with a safer foothold (the hybrid protects fridge/dw from drift); (c) kettle/wm MAP polish (8 vs 32-state delta suggests the blind-chain bits helped kettle/wm slightly - a hybrid state space is worth one A/B).

description:
EXP-16 v16 = v15 + two corrections, both pre-registered in the model docstring BEFORE the run. (1) Rule B posterior-LIVENESS: a chain joins the MAP output only if its ON head crosses its own calib gate on calib ON sessions (on_p95 > gate_thr). Microwave calib sigON p95 = 0.00 - a dead head whose shifted posterior hovers at the decision boundary, making its MAP state pure penalty noise with no timing signal -> routes to the direct v5 path. (2) The joint MAP spans ALL five chains again (v11-style physical state space: the aggregate contains every load; sum-to-aggregate emissions more faithful), while only the OUTPUT routing changes (Rule A visibility AND Rule B liveness).

PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION vs ACTUAL (the prediction was written into the docstring and this design before the bench ran):
- kettle = v11-exact: predicted F1 0.302 / MAE 14.5 -> actual 0.302 / 14.5 (230 preds, 80 matches)
- microwave = v5-exact: predicted 0.018 / 12.6 -> actual 0.018 / 12.6 (73 preds, 3 matches)
- fridge = v5-exact: predicted 0.146 / 43.2 -> actual 0.146 / 43.2 (17564 preds, 3325 matches, bit-identical episode counts)
- washing_machine = v11-exact: predicted 0.335 / 62.6 -> actual 0.335 / 62.6 (1853 preds, 806 matches)
- dishwasher = v5-exact: predicted 0.030 / 30.7 -> actual 0.030 / 30.7 (1750 preds, 46 matches)
The exact match (including episode counts) confirms the component-provenance model: same seed + same calib -> each routed path reproduces its source run bit-for-bit.

METRICS vs v15 (mainline) and v5: min_device_f1 0.017910 vs 0.010152 (+76%) and vs 0.007188 (+149%); mean_device_f1 0.166073 vs 0.156883 (+5.9%, best; v5 0.082936 +100%); pooled_episode_f1 0.156664 vs 0.154406 (+1.5%, best); mean_mae_w 32.69 vs 34.29 (-4.6%; v5 42.53, -23%); worst_mae_w 62.62 vs 67.70 (-7.5%; v5 101.04, -38%); mean_nmae 0.09533 vs 0.09997 (-4.6%); coverage_pred 0.509 vs 0.533 (true 0.258).

Routing print (calib-derived, the decision surface): vis {kettle 4.69, mw 3.20, fridge 0.18, wm 3.58, dw 0.25}, live {kettle T, mw F, fridge T, wm T, dw T} -> mode {kettle MAP, mw direct, fridge direct, wm MAP, dw direct}.

WHY KEEP: every metric better than v15; the improvement is a recomposition of MEASURED components under calib-only rules (no new tuning); the pre-registration protocol (predict -> run -> compare) is the strongest anti-overfit evidence available - the eval table confirmed a prediction made without it, rather than being tuned to.

ANTI-OVERFIT STATEMENT: both routing rules read ONLY calib-session sigmoid statistics and source-house sigma; no eval-span GT statistics entered the design or the routing; the pre-registered per-device prediction was stated before the run and matched exactly. Expanded-eval verification (BENCH_EVAL=90d diagnostic outside the plugin, since the plugin only accepts 'bash .auto/measure.sh') is now DUE on the mainline before further big jumps.

NEXT: min device is again microwave at 0.018 - a dead head (calib ON p95 0.00) that no decode-side mechanism can repair; the remaining levers are (a) i19 self-training on pre-split aggregate to revive the mw/dw ON heads (now safer: fridge/dw/mw outputs are all direct-path, drift-bounded), (b) kettle/wm MAP polish (the 32-state restoration recovered the last of the v11 gains; little left there), (c) 90d expanded-eval diagnostic on this mainline first - it is the cheapest guard against 30d-specific overfit and should precede any new mechanism.

description:
EXP-17 v17 = base-load-adaptive input representation: per-window centered rolling-median subtraction (BASE_WIN 51 samples ~ 5.1 min) applied identically in pretrain, calib and predict (one shared _prep_win transform; unsupervised, no labels, no eval-derived parameters). Root-cause motivation: the cross-house feature shift (mw/dw heads dead on target calib) plausibly comes from the encoder seeing raw house level/base. Preceded by the 90d expanded-eval diagnostic on the v16 mainline (outside the plugin, last_bench.json backed up and restored): min 0.0232 on 90d vs 0.0179 on 30d, pooled 0.159, MAE 33.4 - NO 30d-specific overfit; kettle precision decays 0.348 -> 0.225 over the longer span.

RESULT: COLLAPSE. min_device_f1 0.000000 (dishwasher: 1 pred, 0 matches, MAE 810 W); mean_device_f1 0.072119 (v16: 0.166073); pooled 0.038648 (v16: 0.156664); mean_mae_w 253.00 (v16: 32.69); worst 810.28; mean_nmae 0.737693; coverage_pred_share 3.719321 = 14x the true 0.258 - the direct path fired on most of the span.

CALIB READOUT (the mechanism, printed by the run): the transform destroyed ON/OFF separability everywhere - kettle sigON p05/p50/p95 0.39/0.44/0.65 vs sigOFF 0.46/0.64 (was 0.01/0.93/1.00 vs 0.00/0.84); fridge 0.47-0.51 vs 0.51-0.52 (dead); washing_machine 0.38-0.52 vs 0.50-0.52; dishwasher 0.63-0.67 vs 0.67 (degenerate; med_pred 1982 W vs med_true 122 W - its power head learned nonsense). Gates became midpoints of overlapping distributions (0.45-0.65) -> the gate passes nearly everything -> direct-path watts = power head x max_w x amp_scale nearly everywhere -> 3.7x energy coverage. The MAP devices degraded too (kettle 0.168, wm 0.161) because their posteriors lost separability at the source. val_mse_full 0.18285 (v16: 0.14412), val_mse_on 0.00490 (comparable) - the power head still fits ON amplitudes, but the ON heads lost their decision boundary.

MECHANISM CONCLUSION: absolute-level features are LOAD-BEARING for the v5-architecture heads at the 12-epoch/40k-window budget - the ON heads' dominant feature was the raw level (input > ~2 kW -> kettle), not step shape. Removing the level without adding training budget or capacity to relearn pattern detection collapses separability. The base-subtraction idea is not inherently wrong (the audit's z-norm evidence stands) but requires either (a) keeping the level channel too, or (b) a much longer training schedule.

WHY DISCARD: primary 0.000 << mainline 0.017910; every secondary collapsed. The negative result is design memory: any future representation change must preserve the level channel or retrain longer.

NEXT (ranked): (a) 2-channel input [raw + base-subtracted] - keeps the load-bearing level features AND adds the level-free view; requires Net first-conv in_channels 1 -> 2 (model-owned change) + the same _prep_win helper; (b) longer schedule for the base-subtracted representation (EPOCHS is model-owned; 24-36 epochs doubles training time ~ 90 s); (c) i19 self-training on pre-split aggregate for the dead mw/dw heads (still queued; the mainline is protected by output routing). The 90d diagnostic result is now baseline context: the mainline generalizes across the span.

description:
EXP-18 v18 = two-channel input from the SAME raw window via one shared _prep2 helper used identically in pretrain (build_pool), calib and predict: ch0 = raw/INPUT_SCALE (the exact v16 level-bearing input), ch1 = (raw - centered rolling-median base BASE_WIN=51 ~ 5.1 min)/INPUT_SCALE (level-free step view). Net first conv in_channels 1 -> 2; everything else unchanged (seed, EPOCHS 12, 40k-window budget, decode family, routing). Scale consistency is structural - both channels derive from the same raw watts.

FIRST, THE RUN-17 CORRECTION (record hygiene): run-17's collapse was confounded by a scale bug - build_pool scales pretrain windows by INPUT_SCALE itself, so the v17 _prep_win was applied to ALREADY-SCALED pretrain windows but to RAW watts in calib/predict (~1000x pretrain-vs-inference mismatch). Run-17's "absolute-level features are load-bearing" attribution is WITHDRAWN; the representation hypothesis was untested until now. This run is the clean test.

RESULT: primary min_device_f1 0.005988 (v16 0.017910) -> DISCARD, but the strongest secondary profile of the whole campaign: pooled_episode_f1 0.212086 (v16 0.156664, +35%, best ever; v5 0.129835); fridge F1 0.257 (v16 0.146, +76%, best ever; 20711 preds/6275 matches vs 17564/3325 - both P 0.303 and R 0.224 up); washing_machine 0.326 (v16 0.335, held; MAE 40.9 vs 62.6 - big regression win); worst_mae_w 47.92 (v16 62.62, best since v5-family); mean_device_f1 0.159717 (v16 0.166073); mean_mae_w 33.75 (v16 32.69); mean_nmae 0.098420; coverage_pred 0.475154. val_mse_full 0.12181 (v16 0.14412) - the 2-ch encoder fits better. Per-device: kettle 0.196/27.9 (507 preds/79 matches - P 0.156, down from 0.348), microwave 0.006/10.1 (72 preds/1 match), fridge 0.257/41.9, washing_machine 0.326/40.9, dishwasher 0.013/47.9 (11893 preds - 6.8x v16's 1750 - P 0.007).

CALIB READOUT: microwave head STILL DEAD on calib (sigON p05/p50/p95 = 0.00/0.00/0.00, on_p95 0.00) - the level-free channel did NOT revive it; routed direct as before. Dishwasher gate DEGENERATE: sigON 0.00/0.01/1.00 (huge variance) -> gate 0.05 -> over-fire 11893 preds. Kettle gate dropped to 0.39 (sigOFF p95 0.77 overlaps sigON p05 0.00) -> more FPs. Fridge/wm gates healthier than v16 (fridge 0.46 vs 0.49 sigOFF - borderline; wm 0.94 clean). Routing unchanged (vis identical - sigma/amps calib-derived; live F for mw only).

MECHANISM READING: (1) the level-free channel genuinely helps LOW-AMPLITUDE devices - fridge is the only pure-continuity device and its detection is exactly what the base-shift was hiding; this is the audit's z-norm insight confirmed, now cleanly measured. (2) The channel also helps the aggregate fit (pooled 0.212, wm MAE) but HURTS kettle precision - the base-subtracted view makes mid-size kettle-like residual draws more confusable. (3) The min devices (mw/dw) are NOT representation-limited: mw is head-liveness-limited (dead on calib = needs target-distribution training, i19), dw is gate-liveness/gate-degeneracy-limited. Fixing representation again will not lift the min.

WHY DISCARD: primary 0.0060 << 0.0179 (mw) and dw 0.013 << 0.030; the keep-rule is strict min_device_f1. The fridge/pooled gains are real design memory for a later combination.

NEXT (ranked): (a) i19 self-training on pre-split aggregate for the dead mw head (root fix - target-distribution training; guardrails: freeze encoder, calib early-stop, gate-drift watch) - now even more attractive since the encoder quality is not the bottleneck; (b) 2-ch + a calib-only gate floor for degenerate-gate devices (dw gate 0.05 with sigON p50 0.01 - the gate midpoint rule fails when the calib distribution is degenerate; a floor like max(gate, quantile-derived) is calib-derived, no eval info); (c) re-run the 2-ch variant with kettle precision guard (e.g. kettle direct path instead of MAP) - only if (a)/(b) fail.

description:
EXP-19 v19 = synthetic context-mixing fine-tune of the dead microwave head (design in the model docstring): quiet backgrounds mined from the UNLABELED pre-split aggregate (.auto/cache/house_1_pre.npz 'mains' key ONLY - target GT channels never read, disclosed), source-house mw waveforms (sanctioned pretrain labels) injected scaled to the target calib ON amplitude, mw-only loss, encoder frozen. Implementation shipped a shape bug: the mw slices pm/om are (B,128) but the targets were stored (B,128,1) -> RuntimeError on the FIRST FT batch (512 vs 128 at dim 1), before any optimizer step.

RESULT: the documented fallback engaged exactly as designed - the run is BIT-IDENTICAL to v16: min_device_f1 0.017910, mean 0.166073, pooled 0.156664, mean_mae_w 32.6934, worst 62.624, mean_nmae 0.095326, coverage_pred 0.509042; per-device kettle 0.302/14.5, mw 0.018/12.6, fridge 0.146/43.2, wm 0.335/62.6, dw 0.030/30.7; calib gates identical (0.43/0.05/0.23/0.77/0.05); routing identical. FT note printed: 'error:RuntimeError:...'.

DIAGNOSTIC VALUE: (1) the fallback path is verified bit-exact (try/except + printed note); (2) the data-mining pipeline WORKS - the crash happened inside the FT training loop, so segs/quiet/high pools were non-empty and amp_cal > 0 (the guards passed); (3) a net.train() mode leak into the calib forward is harmless for this architecture (no BN/dropout - gates bit-identical anyway); the fix adds net.eval() to the except handler regardless. (4) The FT'd-head predictions could NOT be tested this run.

FIX (run 20): store FT targets as (N,128) 2D (matching the (B,128) mw slices) instead of (N,128,1); no design change - the docstring pre-registration stands: if the head comes alive on calib, mw routes MAP and F1 should rise well above 0.018; if it stays dead, run ~ v16.

WHY DISCARD: no new mechanism was tested - the run burned on an implementation bug; logging it keeps the append-only history honest. The v16 mainline is untouched (HEAD 8f54897).

description:
EXP-20 = v19 fixed (run-19's shape bug: FT targets now (N,128) 2D matching the (B,128) mw slices; no design change). Mechanism: synthetic context-mixing fine-tune of the dead microwave head - quiet backgrounds mined from the UNLABELED pre-split aggregate, SOURCE-house mw waveforms (sanctioned pretrain labels) injected scaled to the target calib ON amplitude (1588 W), mw-only loss, encoder frozen, other filters receive exactly zero gradient. Data: FT note 'ok amp_cal=1588W segs=496 quiet=2626 high=330' - 496 source mw segments, 2626 quiet + 330 high-draw background windows mined. NO eval GT anywhere; no eval-derived parameters; pre-split npz read mains-key only (disclosed in docstring). Pretrain curves identical to v16 (val_mse_full 0.14412) - the FT runs after pretrain.

RESULT vs v16 (8f54897): min_device_f1 0.029649 vs 0.017910 (+65.6%; the min device is now dishwasher 0.030, microwave rose above it). mean_device_f1 0.173872 vs 0.166073. pooled_episode_f1 0.156676 vs 0.156664 (flat). mean_mae_w 32.9102 vs 32.6934 (+0.22 W, negligible). worst_mae_w 61.50 vs 62.62 (better). mean_nmae 0.095958 vs 0.095326 (flat). coverage_pred 0.511147 vs 0.509042 (flat).

PER-DEVICE: kettle 0.310/11.9 (v16 0.302/14.5 - slightly better F1 and MAE via joint-MAP perturbation), microwave 0.048/17.3 (v16 0.018/12.6; 234 preds/12 matches vs 73/3 - recall 0.011->0.046, 4x), fridge 0.146/43.2 BIT-IDENTICAL (17564 preds/3325 matches - exact, pre-registered), washing_machine 0.336/61.5 (v16 0.335/62.6 - held, 810 vs 806 matches), dishwasher 0.030/30.7 BIT-IDENTICAL (1750/46 - exact, pre-registered).

PRE-REGISTRATION COMPARISON: (1) 'fridge/dishwasher bit-identical' - CONFIRMED EXACTLY (episode counts included), verifying the zero-grad/Adam-zero-step argument. (2) 'kettle/wm ~ v16 small perturbation' - CONFIRMED. (3) 'if the head comes alive on calib, mw routes MAP and F1 rises; if it stays dead the run reproduces v16' - PARTIALLY WRONG IN AN INFORMATIVE WAY: the mw head did NOT come alive on calib (sigON p95 still 0.00, live[mw]=False, mw stayed DIRECT), yet mw F1 rose 2.7x anyway through the direct path. The FT shifted the head's behavior on eval-like contexts (flat-base ~1.6 kW steps) while the 5 real calib mw sessions (noisier context) still do not cross the gate. FINDING: the calib-liveness readout is BLIND to this class of improvement - the 5 calib windows under-represent the contexts where the FT'd head now fires. Readout implication: liveness routing for mw stays OFF, which is currently fine (direct path works), but any future MAP routing for mw cannot rely on this readout.

MECHANISM READING: target-distribution training works where decode-side repairs failed (runs 14/15) - the head needed to see house_1-like aggregate context, and synthetic mixing supplied it legally. The mw head now fires 3.2x more often on the eval span with 4x the true matches; precision is still low (0.051) - the head fires on ~1.6 kW steps that are not mw (residual attribution), the same failure mode as v15's MAP-mw but at much lower amplitude stakes on the direct path.

WHY KEEP: genuine primary improvement (+66% min), every device >= v16, no secondary collapse (worst MAE better, mean MAE +0.22 W, pooled flat), mechanism-level change with a legal data path, pre-registered. New mainline = v19.

NEXT (ranked): (1) 90d expanded-eval verification of THIS mainline (due for a +66% keep - the kettle 90d precision decay seen on v16 needs rechecking); (2) dishwasher is the new min (0.030): its gate is degenerate (sigON 0.00/0.00/1.00 -> gate 0.05) - the same synthetic context-mixing recipe applied to the dw head (its bimodal 122/2360 W amplitudes need two-class synthesis or low/high split) is the obvious next mechanism; (3) mw precision: confidence-filter the direct-path mw output or shrink the injection amplitude band.

description:
EXP-21 = v20: v19's mw context-mix FT kept unchanged, PLUS the same recipe applied to the dishwasher head (now the min at 0.030). Design (docstring pre-registered): source dw ON sessions yield <=128-sample excerpts (2/session, half anchored at onset), scaled per-house by s_h = calib-high-median / source-high-median (house_2 102/2001 W -> ~1.17x, house_5 97/1662 W -> ~1.41x; lands low mode at 119/137 W vs target 122), injected into quiet pre-split backgrounds; high-draw (>=1900 W, majority kettle) negatives teach kettle-blip rejection; dw-only loss, encoder frozen, zero gradient elsewhere. description:
EXP-22 = v21: calib-only bimodal-gate fallback - when the calib ON sigmoid is bimodal-degenerate (on_p50 < 0.10 AND on_p95 > 0.50), the gate recomputes at the midpoint of the OFF ceiling and the ON firing envelope, (on_p95 + off_p95)/2, instead of the collapsed GATE_MIN floor. Trigger set exactly as pre-registered: ONLY dishwasher (p50 0.00/p95 1.00 -> gate 0.50); kettle 0.43 / mw 0.05 / fridge 0.23 / wm 0.77 unchanged (their readouts fail the trigger). No eval data anywhere; trigger thresholds are fixed design constants; the rule derives from target-house calib sigmoid quantiles only.

RESULT vs v19 (67ce270): min_device_f1 0.005054 vs 0.029649 (-83%). dw (the experiment): preds 1750->230 (-87%, as pre-registered) but matches 46->4 - P 0.017, R 0.003, F1 0.030->0.005, MAE 30.7->19.4. Controls: mw 234/12 F1 0.048 BIT-IDENTICAL; fridge 17564/3325 F1 0.146 BIT-IDENTICAL; kettle 222/83 F1 0.319 (v19 210/79 0.310 - slightly BETTER); wm 1878/823 F1 0.340 (v19 1860/810 0.336 - slightly better) - the dw logit shift logit(0.05)->logit(0.50) perturbed the shared MAP traceback favorably. Secondaries: pooled 0.160137 (v19 0.156676, better), mean_mae_w 30.8226 (32.9102, better - fewer FP watts), mean_nmae 0.089871 (0.095958, better), coverage_pred 0.477727 (0.511147, less over-coverage), mean_device_f1 0.171540 (0.173872, flat), worst_mae 61.99 (~61.50).

DIAGNOSIS (design memory, high value): the dw head's 46 real eval-span detections are produced by WEAK firings (sigmoid 0.05-0.50); at gate 0.50 only 4 survive. The strong calib firings (sigON p95 1.00) are an artifact of the 5 calib windows (high-mode episodes over-represented there vs the blip-dominated eval GT). FP/TP separation for dw is NOT in the head's confidence - threshold-based FP reduction is a DEAD END; a gate sweep would be eval-tuning and is forbidden. dw TP signal lives at low confidence in the raw-aggregate representation; only a representation change (e.g. the level-free channel making 122 W relative steps visible) or context features outside the raw aggregate can move dw.

WHY DISCARD: primary -83%; the pre-registered success condition (high-mode firings carry the TPs) is refuted. Keep/discard is by the 30d primary per protocol - despite 4 secondaries improving, the min collapsed. Auto-reverts to v19.

NEXT: run-18's table (.auto/runs/18.log) shows the two-channel dw head had 87 matches (R 0.064, ~2x the 1-ch 46) at gate 0.05 and fridge 0.257 (+76%), pooled 0.212 - the level-free channel carries real dw signal. description: EXP-26 (v25): source-pool feed repair - build_pool now gathers windows from _ffill0(source mains) = ffill(limit 10)+fillna(0), the bench's own inference preprocessing, instead of raw mains. DIAGNOSIS (preflight, source data only): raw source mains is chopped by p50-length-1 NaN dropouts every ~27 valid samples, so _valid_starts saw 0.5-1.7% of the span; the old pool ran at 16,247/40k windows from unrepresentative pockets (house_2 pockets: dw 98% ON within mask -> dw pos_w 1.0, zero OFF examples -> over-fire 1750 preds P 0.026). PRE-REGISTRATION: pool 40,000 windows; pos_w {k 50, mw 50, fr ~1.4, wm ~38, dw ~41}; dw preds down from 1750, dw F1 two-sided (min-bearer); other rows two-sided; KEEP iff min >= 0.0296 AND mean_device_f1 >= 0.196. CONFIRMED IN-RUN: pool train exactly 40000 {house_2 25247, house_5 14753}, val 8000; pos_w {k 50.0, mw 50.0, fr 1.4, wm 39.4, dw 41.7}. EVAL vs run-24: kettle 150/82/0.547P/0.365 F1/6.0 MAE (was 211/79/0.310/11.9 - BIG improvement), microwave 775/121/0.233/44.2 (was 116/9/0.048/11.6 - F1 x4.8, recall 0.034->0.462, MAE worse), washing_machine 1574/871/0.384/45.9 (was 1860/810/0.336/61.5 - improved, no longer worst-MAE), fridge 3750/703/0.044/45.2 (was 20711/6275/0.257/41.9 - CRASH: ch2 fridge sigON 0.63-0.82 ~ sigOFF 0.60-0.68, head degenerated to near-constant ~0.65-0.73, R 0.224->0.025), dishwasher 1618/16/0.011/83.8 (was 1750/46/0.030/30.7 - head INVERTED: ch1 dw calib sigON p50 0.12 vs sigOFF p50 0.78 - fires on OFF, silent on ON; amp med_pred 92W vs med_true 122W). min_device_f1 0.010771 (dw) < 0.0296 -> DISCARD per pre-registration. mean_device_f1 0.207466 > 0.196 (kettle/mw/wm gains outweigh fridge/dw crashes) - the repaired pool is strictly better training data for the event-like devices. val_mse endpoints: ch1 0.14880 (vs run-24 0.14412), ch2 0.12030 (vs 0.12181) - NOT comparable: the val pool itself changed (8000 whole-span windows vs the old pocket-derived ~2k); the eval table is the arbiter. Duration 584 s (2.5x data as expected). MECHANISM CONCLUSIONS: (1) the pool repair is real and valuable - kettle/mw/wm all improved on representative training data; (2) source fridge labels outside the old raw-valid pockets are harmful: the old pocket-trained fridge was the campaign's best (0.257), the whole-span-trained fridge degenerated to a constant sigmoid (0.044) - source fridge GT quality is span-dependent; (3) source dw labels transfer INVERTED with balanced pos_w (fires on target OFF, silent on target ON) - 5th independent dw refutation: source dw GT convention appears misaligned with the target's (house_2 dw channel carries long ~2kW draws, target dw is 122 W blips), beyond gating/FT/representation/signal-class. NEXT (EXP-27 candidate): per-device span gating grounded in SOURCE-data evidence - verify on source channels only that fridge/dw label statistics inside vs outside the raw-valid pockets differ structurally; if confirmed, gate the fridge/dw loss masks to pocket-overlapping windows while kettle/wm/mw keep the full-span pool (keeps the kettle/mw/wm gains, restores the pocket-trained fridge, dw stays capped). Anti-cheat: source-only data; FFILL=10 is the bench's frozen inference constant, not a tuned knob; no eval GT anywhere.

description: EXP-27 (v26): re-applied the run-26 pool repair and added per-device span gating - POCKET_GATED={'fridge','dishwasher'} heads train only on fully-raw-mains-valid windows (exactly the pre-v25 pool: all 16,247 raw-valid windows), kettle/microwave/washing_machine on the full 40,000 (16,247 pocket + 23,753 whole-span from the _ffill0 feed). RATIONALE: run-26 showed the whole-span pool lifts kettle/mw/wm (0.310->0.365/0.048->0.233/0.336->0.384) but crashes fridge (0.257->0.044) and inverts dw; the pocket regime is the proven fridge/dw configuration. IN-RUN: pools exactly as registered (train 40000 = pocket 16247 + whole-span 23753; val 8000 = 3774 + 4226); pos_w {k 50, mw 50, fr 1.3, wm 42.6, dw 1.0} - gated heads back to the old regime. EVAL: kettle 253/79/0.312P/0.286F1/12.1 MAE (run-26 0.365 -> LOST: the 16,247 pocket windows re-entered kettle training), microwave 694/126/0.264/25.5 (gain kept, above run-26's 0.233), fridge 10485/1705/0.089/45.4 (partial recovery from 0.044, far below run-24's 0.257; ch2 fridge sigON 0.17-0.29 ~ sigOFF 0.20-0.30 - still near-constant), washing_machine 1387/757/0.348/36.4 (kept most of 0.384), dishwasher 13151/122/0.009P/0.017F1/53.1 (over-fire regime: 13,151 preds, worse than run-24's 46-pred 0.030). min_device_f1 0.016823 < 0.0296 -> DISCARD. mean 0.200597, pooled 0.094729, mean_mae 34.51, worst 53.12 (dw), nmae 0.1006. MECHANISM CONCLUSION: the two pool regimes are NOT composable through loss-mask gating - the gated heads inherit the shared encoder that the mixed pool shapes, and run-24's fridge/dw heads were joint products of (pool, encoder), neither reproducible by masking alone; conversely kettle/wm lose part of their whole-span gains when 40% of the pool reverts to pockets. This is the 3rd pool-family data point (runs 24/26/27). CONTEXT: this run lands amid an external review (user-forwarded) alleging the benchmark itself is unlearnable (GT episode flicker fragmentation; claimed smoothed-perfect ceiling fridge 0.043 / dw 0.006, below our best min 0.030) - ceiling verification scheduled next; the dw/fridge 'structural cap' conclusions in runs 18-26 may be artifacts of a broken metric rather than model limits. ft_pre/ft_post = 0.17446 (ch2 end-pretrain val_mse_full, new pool). Duration 493 s.
