description:
Run 104: the wm admission floors' fragility (m39's recorded lead) is NOT the over-emission mechanism. Both halves tested and refuted.

MOTIVATION (from .auto/runs/102.log): _wm30_profile's two admission FLOORS are plain mins over the five usable mark windows - hs_band = (0.75*min(hss), 1.75*max(hss)) and dens_lo = 0.75*min(denss). In the logged builds the density floor reached 0.068-0.151/min, BELOW the 0.184/min dw30 run ceiling that the docstring says this floor exists to reject, and hs_lo rounded to 0.00 in 3 builds (making the heat-share test vacuous for that whole house). hs is measured over the MERGED run, so a build with a large max_gap yields long low-hs merged runs that simultaneously loosen the floor and widen the merge - merge_n and hs_lo co-vary. The file's own precedent for one anomalous window is ext_back_s using a median (L729-735).

CHANGE (model.py, 9 insertions / 1 deletion as pooled): replace 0.75*min(x) with 0.75*(sorted(x)[1] if len(x) >= 3 else min(x)) for hs_band[0] and dens_lo - a trimmed min (second-weakest of five windows), plus a docstring correction of the 'the marks' min run density' claim.

SCREEN (seed 2026, 19 s each): bundle (both trimmed) 0.372409 vs the blunt rule's 0.373461 (-0.001052), wm median 0.247979 -> 0.242229. Split: (A) density-trim only 0.373607 (+0.000146), wm 0.247885 (-0.000094), kettle 0.567582 (+0.000873), house_1 0.526951 (-0.002477); (B) heat-share-trim only 0.372577 (-0.000884), wm 0.243702 (-0.004277), house_1 0.532603 (+0.003175). So the HEAT-SHARE trim is the harmful half and the density trim is noise at this draw.

POOL (5 seeds, 150.2 s, checks pass, variant A = density trim only): primary 0.366174 - BIT-IDENTICAL to the committed blunt rule on every reported aggregate (p10 0.345739, device_balanced 0.368405, house_1 0.529428, kettle 0.561050, mw 0.267210, fridge 0.387253, wm 0.246657, dw 0.384353). The change therefore fires only in the seed-2026 calibration draw; since the primary is the median of the five per-seed means (and the other aggregates are medians over seeds), a single-draw effect cannot move any of them.

INTERPRETATION. (1) The heat-share floor is a RECALL guard, not a precision guard: the low-hs merged runs it admits are real wm cycles with long pump phases, so trimming it costs 0.0043 of wm median - m39's lead was mis-framed, and the floor's looseness in 3 builds is protecting truth, not admitting lookalikes. Do not reopen it. (2) The density floor rarely binds at all on this pool: after trimming it, 4 of the 5 seeds are unchanged to the last digit, so the dw30-lookalike rejection is already achieved by the other gates (span/amp/mean/idle ceilings) wherever it matters. (3) METHOD: a seed-2026 screen is not a valid go/no-go filter for a change whose firing depends on the calibration draw - the primary is a median over seeds and seed 2026 is the top, most atypical draw (0.373 vs 0.346-0.366 for seeds 1-4). Before spending a 150 s pool run, check whether a change fires in a MID seed (e.g. --seeds 1 or 3), not only in 2026. This is the first run where the screen and the pool disagreed in sign (screen +0.0001, pool exactly 0.000000).

Bar stays 0.376174.

description:
Run 105: decouple the wm detector's heat level from the dishwasher's mark. REFUTED as a primary gain; recorded for its device-coupling finding.

HYPOTHESIS: _wm30_profile mined its candidate runs at heat = PROG_HEAT_AMP_FRAC * min(mark_wm['amp'], dw_amp) - a CROSS-DEVICE coupling. In any house whose dw mark reads below its wm mark, the wm run-basis dropped onto the dishwasher's weaker heater excursions and mined dw-level runs as wm candidates, leaving their rejection entirely to the gates (the same gates whose density floor run 104 showed rarely binds). The wm's own mark is the physically correct anchor.

CHANGE (model.py, 5 insertions / 1 deletion): heat = PROG_HEAT_AMP_FRAC * mark_wm['amp'], plus a 4-line rationale comment. ast-verified.

SCREENS. seed 3 (the MEDIAN seed = the primary's own draw; base mean 0.366174): variant 0.366222 (+0.000048). Per-device: microwave 0.267210 -> 0.292094 (+0.024884), dishwasher 0.384353 -> 0.354751 (-0.029602), kettle 0.561050 -> 0.561931 (+0.000881), wm 0.246657 -> 0.246163 (-0.000494), fridge +0.000219, house_1 0.529428 -> 0.529074, device_balanced 0.368405 -> 0.368482. seed 2026: 0.373461 -> 0.373596 (+0.000135), with mw and dw BIT-IDENTICAL to base (0.263486 / 0.424824) and the movement in kettle (+0.000632), house_1 (+0.005652) and wm (+0.000088).

POOL (5 seeds): see metrics. The change fires (it is not inert like run 104's density trim) but its effects are a near-exact cancellation: at the median seed the microwave's +0.024884 is offset by the dishwasher's -0.029602, and at seed 2026 both devices are unchanged. Every aggregate stays within ~0.001 of the committed rule, i.e. noise, and nowhere near the 0.376174 bar.

FINDING (the durable part). A wm change is NOT device-local. The wm30 runs are emitted as program spans and enter the shared prog_spans / dispute / named-chain machinery that gates the microwave, dishwasher and kettle, so editing the wm's candidate generation reorders the microwave and dishwasher medians by up to 0.03 in a single draw. Consequences for the standing work: (1) any wm-only hypothesis must be judged on the device medians of the OTHER devices too, never on the wm median alone; (2) a device-local-looking gain of ~0.025 in one draw can be a pure reallocation with zero net effect, which is why the primary (a median over seeds of the mean over 66 pairs) is the only admissible arbiter; (3) the run-102 program-span rule is the coupling channel, so any future change to it must be evaluated on all five device medians.

description:
Run 106: cap the wm's idle ceiling at the level the run was detected at.

EVIDENCE (full pool profile dump, seed 2026): _wm30_profile builds 'idle_hi': 2.0 * max(idles) where idles[i] is the MEDIAN of the sub-level phase inside the i-th merged run (L722 = float(np.median(below))). Since a merged run is by construction the 30 s grid at or above heat, EVERY idle value is below heat - the ceiling can only exceed the run-detection level through the 2.0 factor, and in the dump it does: idle<=2952 W and <=2914 W in two houses, and 263 W in a house whose own heat is 161 W (0.75 x its 215 W mark amp). A ~3 kW 'quiet level' test admits anything, so a gate meant to require a genuinely quiet pump/electronics phase between heater blocks is vacuous exactly where the wm over-emits (pool wm precision 0.245; 7/15 pairs under F1 0.2).
